---
title: "Annotations, comments and the inbox"
subtitle: "Point at anything, choose an agent, and follow the conversation"
---

Annotations combine your note with exactly what you were looking at. Paper margin
comments stay attached to document text. Both appear in **Inbox**, where you can reply,
choose who handles each item, and see its status. Reader PDF **Highlights** remain in
[your reference library](../modes/reader.qmd); annotate a passage to bring it into Inbox.

# Point out what needs attention

- **Margin comments** anchor a discussion to document text.
- **Ctrl+Shift+M** opens **Annotate** in Figure, Paper, Slide, Library, Reader, Present,
  and utility windows. Your current selection becomes a target chip. Type immediately:
  the note keeps keystrokes even while the frozen view is being captured.
- **Annotate…** is also in the global and Paper palettes and Library's **Commands…** menu.
- In Reader, select PDF text or open a saved highlight and click **✦ Annotate this passage**
  to prefill a passage target.

## Point, type, add {#sec-annotate}

The frozen view fills the window, with drawing tools at the top left and a focused note
at the bottom right. Hover to see the target's outline and name: a plot series, text box,
figure, caption, paragraph, slide, animation clip, PDF passage, or reference.

**Drag** to draw a numbered arrow. **Alt+A**, **Alt+B**, and **Alt+P** select arrow, box,
and pen. An arrow names its tip's target; a box names the objects inside; a pen names its
starting target. **Alt+Z** undoes a mark. Use **Alt+↑ / ↓** or the wheel to widen/narrow the
hovered target; each chip also has widening and remove controls.

**Enter** adds the annotation; **Shift+Enter** inserts a newline. **Escape** or the chord
again closes the surface and keeps the draft and its picture. **Attach view** is on by
default and remembered; drawing marks forces it on. The saved picture is cropped around
marks, or captures the whole window when there are none. If capture is unavailable, the
note still carries targets and marks and tells you there is no screenshot.

If the view changed while a draft was closed, its earlier picture and targets stay together.
Choose **Refresh view (clears marks)** to keep the note and draw on the current view.

## To: choose who receives it

**Inbox** is the default: collect notes until you ask an agent to address them. **Any
watching agent** lets the first watching session claim the item. Choose a connected agent
by name to queue the annotation for that session. Agents that are connected but not watching
appear after watching agents, greyed and marked **queued until it watches**. They remain
selectable. Your choice is remembered per project.

**Tab** in the note cycles recipients. Typing **@any** or **@heron** also sets **To:**;
recognized routing mentions are removed from the saved text. **#tags** appear as chips.
**New background agent** appears when background runs are available ([below](#sec-background)).

## Pair with the live window

Connect with `--live` to pair with the open project. A connected session in live mode
shows **Pairing** in Annotate's **To:** menu; choose its name to hand it an annotation.
An agent can use `get_view` to see the current Flux window and its context, including
while Annotate is open. Each view briefly shows **◉ heron viewed your window** in the
titlebar, using that session's name.

**Settings → General → Allow agents to view the Flux window** is on by default.
Turn it off to refuse agent screenshots. The agent receives a clear disabled message.
Viewing captures only that project's Flux window.

## Inbox: review, reply, and status {#sec-note-popover}
Open **Inbox** from the titlebar (the badge counts open items), **Alt+Q**, or the **Inbox**
command in the command palette. The composer's **Open inbox** link opens the same panel.
It combines annotations with margin comments from every project document. **Pin open**
keeps it in a separate window; **Dock** brings it back without losing a reply draft.

The list groups items into **Needs input**, **Open**, **Claimed**, and a collapsed **Resolved**
section. Type a filter such as `draft_1 #claude figure`; chips show the document, tag, and
surface filters. You can also use `comments`, `annotations`, `figure:Density`, `deck:talk`,
`status:resolved`, or free text. `archived` includes archived items; `all` includes withdrawn
items. The same query works with `flux inbox`.

Select an item to see its full text, picture, numbered anchors, and conversation. **R** focuses
Reply; **Enter** sends, and **Shift+Enter** adds a newline. Agent replies show the agent's name.
**Jump to** returns to the document range, figure selection, slide and beat, or Reader page.
**↑/↓** move between rows; **Enter** on a row jumps; **E** archives. **Unarchive** restores an
archived item, and **Reopen** returns resolved work to the inbox. **Copy agent prompt** copies
an instruction you can give your agent.

**Edit** loads an annotation's original text, targets, and picture; **Add** replaces it while
preserving history. **Withdraw** removes your annotation from the active list. The ledger is
append-only at `.meta/feedback.ndjson`; pictures live in `.meta/feedback/` and are saved before
their notes are published. Replies to margin comments stay in their document's comment sidecar.

Status chips update as agents work: **Queued → heron**, **Claimed by heron**, **heron needs
your input**, and **Resolved by heron**. Toasts name the agent; a question's toast opens that
item in Inbox.

**Assign ▾** (or **A** on a row) uses the same recipients as **To:**. **Unassign** returns
an item to Inbox, where nobody watches it automatically. **Release claim** pulls work back
from its current holder while keeping its route. The released agent receives a notice and
cannot continue writing to that item; explicitly assigning it back authorizes it again.
Reassigning or unassigning held work also releases the previous holder.

If an assignment expires, its chip reads **heron disconnected — reassign?**, and the item
returns to Open with its previous holder retained. Claims stay active while the agent is
connected or has acted on the item in the last 30 minutes; once both expire, they show the
same reassign prompt.

The titlebar's **2 agents ▾** chip and **AI status → Sessions** show the same connected
sessions: name, product and surface, connected-since time, **👁 Watching · queue**,
**👁 Watching · annotations**, or **👁 Watching · filter**, and **🖥 Live** when pairing.
Each row shows pending queue count and current claims. **Copy name** copies the handle;
**Show its items** opens Inbox with that agent's `@name` filter. **Stop watching** ends its
wait and releases its claims. The titlebar chip disappears when no sessions are connected.

## Who gets what: a worked example

1. Two agents are connected: **heron** is watching my annotations; **wren** is connected
   but not watching. Both appear in the titlebar agents chip and **AI status → Sessions**.
2. I annotate a legend with `@wren move this below the axis`. **To:** switches to wren,
   and after I add it the Inbox chip reads **Queued → wren (not watching)**. Heron cannot
   take it. Wren's row shows **1 queued**.
3. I annotate a caption and choose **To: Any watching agent**. Heron claims it, and the
   live chip becomes **Claimed by heron**. Heron's current claim names the caption item.
4. Later I tell wren, “check your queue.” It checks `flux inbox --mine`, claims the legend
   item, and resolves it after moving the legend. A named queue reaches its agent even
   when that agent's watch filter would otherwise exclude the item.
5. The chip becomes **Resolved by wren**, and the toast reads
   **wren resolved: move this below the axis**.

I can change either annotation's recipient with **Assign ▾**, return it to **Inbox** with
**Unassign**, or pull back work in progress with **Release claim**. Nothing starts merely
because an agent is connected; watching and addressing a queue are explicit actions.

# Ask an agent to address your notes

[Connect your agent](connect.qmd), then tell it what to work on. For example:

- “Address my open annotations.”
- “Address all my comments in draft_1.”
- “Address everything tagged #stats in Figure.”
- “Address the annotation I just made.”
- “Check your queue.”

The agent reads the item, its picture, targets and thread, claims it, and replies or
resolves it after checking its work. **Needs input** means it has a question for you;
reply in the Inbox thread. Tags help filter work; a **#claude** tag alone does not assign
an item to Claude. Use **To:** or **Assign ▾** to choose the recipient.

## Watch mode

Say “watch my annotations,” “watch my queue,” or “watch annotations tagged #stats.”
Watching is opt-in and lasts until you tell the agent to stop or choose **Stop watching**
in Sessions. Connecting alone never starts it.

A watcher receives items routed to **Any watching agent** that match its scope, plus
items assigned to its own name even outside that filter. Queue-only watching receives
its named queue. **Inbox** items stay passive until you explicitly ask an agent to
address them. With several watchers, the first successful claim owns an Any item.

For agents, the waiting tool is `wait_for_inbox`; the CLI twin is `flux wait-inbox`.
These return the request, targets, picture and thread together. Agents claim before
working, respect reassignment and release, and ask in the thread when they need input.
See the [CLI reference](../reference/cli.qmd) for the complete tool reference.

## Ask about what you see

Press **Ctrl+Shift+J**, choose **Ask about this…** in **Ctrl+K**, or use **Ask** beside
Reader's passage action. The Figure properties menu also offers **✦ Ask**. Ask captures
your current selection and window; type immediately, then press **Enter** to send.
**Shift+Enter** adds a newline. It works in every project surface, including Present and
pinned utility windows.

Choose your installed agent, model, and effort in **Settings → General → Agent that
Flux launches** (also in **AI status → Agents → Agent that Flux launches (Ask)…**). Flux runs your own Claude Code or Codex CLI with your existing login;
usage counts against your plan. Install and sign in using that CLI first. Flux does not
handle vendor logins.

Answers appear in a popover with expandable tool activity showing the actual inputs.
Ask is read-only. **Stop** cancels the run. **Escape** or **Close Ask** discards the
exchange from Flux; the CLI's own session history remains. **Keep** saves the question,
answers, captured view, and targets as a resolved annotation. **Copy resume command**
copies a command you can paste into your own terminal to continue the vendor session.

## Run an item in the background {#sec-background}

Open the **Inbox** (**Alt+Q**), select an open item, and choose **Run in background ▾ →
Claude Code** or **Codex**. Or send a new annotation **To: New background agent**, or
start it with `@new` (Claude Code) or `@new-codex` (Codex). The option appears when
AI status finds an installed, signed-in CLI.

The agent is a session like any other: it appears in **AI status → Sessions** and the
titlebar agents chip with a name such as **bg · claude · wren**, claims the item, and
signs its replies with that name. The item shows a live activity strip with the actual
tool inputs, progress and reported usage. **Stop** (on the strip or the session row)
cancels the run; the item returns to Open, marked "bg · claude · wren disconnected —
reassign?". Replying in the item's thread continues the same session when it can; a
reply sent while the agent is working waits for that turn to finish. If a run ends
without replying or resolving, its last message is added to the thread.

A background agent may edit the project and its analysis workspace. It may run the
`flux` command, and `uv run` in a uv workspace, without asking. Anything else Claude
Code wants to do opens a dialog showing the **exact** command or input: **Allow once**
or **Deny**. Closing the window, or leaving the dialog for two minutes, denies it. Codex
runs with workspace-write access and refuses anything that would need more approval.
Both are told never to push, publish or delete, and to propose those instead.

One agent works on each item. **Agent that Flux launches** (Settings, or AI status)
sets how many background runs go at once (1–3, default 2); further items wait for a
slot. Usage counts against the plan of the CLI you signed in to.

# Troubleshooting

- No agent takes a note → check **To:** and Sessions. An Inbox-only item stays passive;
  a named queue waits until its agent watches or checks it.
- An agent disconnected → use **Assign ▾** to choose another connected session.
- A verb says `deferred: … is locked` → you're mid-edit in the app; the agent retries
  after you finish.
- Ask reports a missing or outdated CLI → install/update it and sign in from your own
  terminal, then reopen Settings. For missing Flux tools, use **AI status → Repair**.
- No screenshot → the annotation still keeps its text and targets; the composer reports
  that capture was unavailable. Check **Attach view** before adding another note.
